keyTerms.definition: Geographic areas holding AZs; picked for latency, law, and service availability.
Identity and Access Management: the system deciding who can do what in AWS.

recall.question: What does this volume cover?
recall.answer: The AWS that AIP-C01 assumes you know: Regions, IAM, S3, EC2, VPC, databases, Lambda, and the services connecting them.

keyTerms.definition: S3 tiers priced by how often you touch the data.
S3 rules that move or delete objects on a schedule.

recall.question: How does AIP-C01 test foundations material?
recall.answer: Never as trivia, always inside a scenario: the cheapest compliant design needs storage classes, lifecycle rules, and KMS together.

sections.title: Watch first: the full foundations course

keyTerms.definition: A geographic area holding two or more AZs; picked for latency, law, and services.
One or more discrete data centers inside a Region, with independent power and network.
Points of presence in hundreds of cities that cache content and answer DNS near users.
On the exam, almost always means running in two or more AZs.
AWS secures the cloud itself; you secure what you put in it.

recall.question: Berlin users, data must stay in the EU, app runs on one EC2 instance in us-east-1a. Smallest fix?
recall.answer: Move the workload to eu-central-1 and run in at least two AZs: the Region must change for data residency, and two AZs give availability.

recall.question: Who patches the OS on EC2, on RDS, on Lambda?
recall.answer: You patch EC2; AWS patches RDS and Lambda. If the service is managed or serverless, AWS owns the OS.

keyTerms.definition: A temporary badge anyone trusted can assume; it hands out keys that die on their own.
A JSON document saying allow or deny on API calls and resources.
A deny in any policy that overrides every allow and ends the request.
A managed policy capping what an identity can ever do, no matter its other policies.
Multi-factor authentication: a second proof of identity, like a code from your phone.

recall.question: A Lambda function uses an access key in an environment variable and the security team flags it. Correct fix?
recall.answer: Attach an IAM role to the function with s3:GetObject on the source bucket and s3:PutObject on the destination; no keys needed.

recall.question: Guarantee that no product-team user can ever delete production databases. Which control?
recall.answer: A permissions boundary on every product-team user and role: team-written policies can never exceed it.

keyTerms.definition: Containers for objects; names are globally unique but each bucket lives in one Region.
99.999999999% durability: S3 copies data across at least three AZs.
Rules that move or delete objects on a schedule without you touching them.
Keeps every version of an object; reverses accidental overwrites and deletes.
A signed link sharing one private object until it expires; the bucket stays private.
Server-side encryption with your KMS keys; every encrypt and decrypt lands in CloudTrail.

recall.question: Fine-tuning datasets: last month read daily, older data audited yearly, keep 7 years. Cheapest design?
recall.answer: A lifecycle rule: keep recent data hot for 30 days, move older data to Glacier Flexible Retrieval, expire after 7 years.

recall.question: Share one private invoice PDF for 24 hours, never publicly listable. How?
recall.answer: Generate a presigned URL with a 24-hour expiry; the bucket stays private the whole time.

keyTerms.definition: Amazon Machine Image: the operating system image an instance launches from.
Spare EC2 capacity at up to 90% off, reclaimable by AWS with a 2-minute warning.
Network-attached disk that persists independently of the instance; snapshot it to S3.
A shared NFS file system for many writers across AZs.
A 1- or 3-year dollar-per-hour commit saving up to 72%, with flexibility to change types.

recall.question: 50 EC2 instances need one shared input folder across two AZs. Which storage fits?
recall.answer: EFS: a shared NFS file system built for many writers across AZs.

recall.question: A nightly 3-hour reporting job is retryable and the CFO wants the lowest price. Which pricing?
recall.answer: Spot instances: the job tolerates interruption, which is exactly what the 2-minute reclaim warning is built for.

keyTerms.definition: Your own isolated network inside AWS; nothing gets in or out unless you build the road.
A one-way door in a public subnet: private subnets reach out, nobody outside reaches in.
A stateful firewall around an instance; allow rules only, and they add up.
A stateless firewall around a subnet; allow and deny rules evaluated in number order.
Private access to AWS services without touching the internet at all.
A serverless key-value store with single-digit millisecond latency at any scale.

recall.question: A Lambda function in private subnets must call an external payment API. Least-exposure fix?
recall.answer: Put a NAT gateway in a public subnet and route 0.0.0.0/0 from the private subnets to it: outbound-only internet.

recall.question: Block one attacking IP at the subnet edge fast, without touching any instance. Which control?
recall.answer: A NACL deny rule with a low rule number: security groups have no deny rules.

recall.question: A mobile leaderboard needs 5 ms reads and writes at 100,000 rps across three Regions, with no DBAs. Which service?
recall.answer: DynamoDB with Global Tables on on-demand capacity: serverless key-value, active-active across Regions.

keyTerms.definition: Asks how healthy it is right now: metrics, alarms, logs, dashboards.
Asks who did what, when: every API call in the account, logged to S3.
Asks whether resources are still configured correctly: compliance rules and history.

recall.question: Which IAM principal modified the production security group yesterday at 3 PM?
recall.answer: CloudTrail: it records every API call with the caller identity and timestamp.

keyTerms.definition: A queue: senders drop messages in, receivers pull them out; it decouples and buffers.
Pub/sub fan-out: publish once to a topic and every subscriber gets a push.
The event bus: rules match events and route them to targets, plus cron schedules.
Catches poison messages that fail repeatedly so they stop blocking workers.

recall.question: An order service must notify warehouse, email, and analytics without coupling them. Which design?
recall.answer: Publish to one SNS topic with each consumer subscribed via SQS or Lambda: fan-out decouples every consumer.

sections.title: 11. API Gateway: the managed front door

keyTerms.definition: Cheap and fast; the fit for Lambda and HTTP backends.
Full features: usage plans, API keys, request mapping, WAF, and caching.
Two-way APIs that stay open, for chat and live feeds.

recall.question: A public API needs per-customer rate limits, API keys for billing tiers, and GET caching. Which option?
recall.answer: A REST API with usage plans, API keys, and caching: HTTP APIs lack usage plans and API keys.

keyTerms.definition: A data key encrypts the file locally and fast; KMS encrypts the data key with the master key.
Your KMS key with your policies, your rotation, and your disable switch.
S3 server-side encryption with your KMS keys; every decrypt lands in CloudTrail.

recall.question: Patient scans in S3 need a log entry for every decryption and instant revoke. Which choice?
recall.answer: SSE-KMS with a customer-managed key: KMS logs every decrypt, and disabling the key revokes everything under it.

keyTerms.definition: The set of resources CloudFormation creates together from one template.
A preview of what an update will change before it runs.
Catches resources that someone hand-edited outside the template.
Deploys one template across many accounts and Regions.

recall.question: Prod and staging drifted apart from console clicks and nobody knows the differences. Permanent fix?
recall.answer: Define the stack in CloudFormation templates, deploy per environment, and run drift detection.

keyTerms.definition: The S3 billing unit: gigabytes stored times the fraction of the month.
Shows where the money went.
Alerts, and can act, when spend crosses a line you set.
Merges accounts through Organizations for one bill and stacked volume discounts.

recall.question: 12 accounts, one bill, volume discounts, per-team breakdowns. Which combination?
recall.answer: AWS Organizations with consolidated billing plus cost allocation tags per team.

sections.title: 15. Putting it together: a GenAI app on AWS

keyTerms.definition: The edge cache serving HTTPS at the front of the architecture.
Roles with exactly the permissions needed and no keys: the function may invoke the model and read one bucket.

recall.question: A scenario says secure GenAI application. What four things do you check, in order?
recall.answer: Network: private subnets plus endpoints. Identity: least-privilege roles, no keys. Data: KMS encryption and versioning. Audit: CloudTrail and CloudWatch.

keyTerms.definition: Share one private file briefly; never open a public bucket.
Caps what a team can ever do, no matter its other policies.
Blocks one IP fast at the subnet edge; security groups cannot deny.

recall.question: A private subnet needs OS patches but must stay unreachable. Which answer?
recall.answer: A NAT gateway in a public subnet, with the private route table pointing at it.

keyTerms.definition: Free private access to S3 or DynamoDB from private subnets.
Makes early deletion impossible, even for root, in compliance mode.
SSO for workforce access across accounts with no long-term keys.

recall.question: A Lambda function in a private subnet times out calling DynamoDB. Cheapest fix?
recall.answer: Add a gateway VPC endpoint for DynamoDB: private subnets get free, private access.

recall.question: Training data must be kept 7 years, read heavily for 30 days, and undeletable before 90 days. Which design?
recall.answer: S3 Standard with a lifecycle rule to Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 30 days, plus Object Lock in compliance mode.

keyTerms.definition: The AWS certification wiki's maintained minimum-viable study path.
The Reddit community holding years of I-passed notes.

recall.question: Where do you go after foundations?
recall.answer: If AI and ML vocabulary feels thin, take the AIF-C01 prereq next; otherwise start the exam proper with D1.
